title: Robot Wrench Frame and Clock Registration With Gap Recovery
output_folder: E:\create_challenge_synthetic_output_folder\sprint_5\Robot Wrench Frame and Clock Registration With Gap Recovery
notes: This was evaluated as a new participant contract, not as a status change to the rejected action/event candidate.
Fixed-microphone audio, action text, action intervals, object identities, and success labels were excluded from both pilots.
Two distinct deidentification designs were attacked before the candidate was rejected.
No output challenge folder, build scripts, forms, upload package, or platform draft was created.

candidate_contract.input: A source-deidentified numeric packet containing robot-motion context and a partially missing six-axis wrench observed in an unknown proper signed-axis frame and with an unknown clock offset.
candidate_contract.output: The sensor-to-base signed axis transform, clock correction, and canonical wrench values only at withheld indices.

multiburst_pilot.row_unit: four shuffled non-contiguous one-second bursts from one recording

metric_null_audit.finding: The transparent coupled metric had a reasonable null floor and kept every one-head oracle below 0.45; metric shape was not the rejection cause.

scale_projection.finding: Projected row and byte capacity looked viable, but full post-filter extraction and exact import were not pursued after two decisive gates failed.

novelty.closest_source_task: REASSEMBLE multimodal temporal action segmentation; the proposed calibration task is different from the source's canonical task.
closest_local_challenges: Wearable Muscle And Motion Stream Reassociation
Bridge Sensor Window Selection and Observability Matrix Prediction
closest_external_work: On the Calibration of Force/Torque Sensors in Robotics
Observability-Aware Intrinsic and Extrinsic Calibration of LiDAR-IMU Systems
novelty.finding: The contract is a union of an accepted clock-offset/cross-modal reassociation solver family and accepted dense sensor-completion families, with a standard force/torque frame-calibration head. The robot domain and JSON/NPZ wrapper do not create substantive novelty.

rejection_reasons: novelty score 4.0/10 is below the required 6/10 threshold
single-window source retrieval recovered 100% of raw windows and 95% of frame transforms
multi-burst deidentification still recovered 99.58% of burst sources and 98.33% of complete row compositions
source-assisted multiburst search recovered 87.22% of frame transforms and 88.89% of clock offsets
the legitimate leave-one-recording-out model did not beat the null metric score on the stronger deidentification, indicating poor learnability after the transformations needed to resist lookup
